newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE may settle back to 4,625.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE may settle back to 4,625.

text.p: Nagging doubts about interest rates will dampen enthusiasm for UK equities on Thursday so that the FTSE will have difficulty going above 4,650 and may dip to 4,625, technical analysts said.

Despite bouncing back on Wednesday after two days of sharp falls, the FTSE had no support from the gilts market where the yield on the 10 year benchmark gilt stock was 7.15 percent compared with 6.95 percent a week ago.
As the gilt yield is not likely to improve today, it will be difficult for the FTSE to forge ahead, analysts said.
By 0725 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 5.9 at 4,636.1.

A daily bar chart of the FTSE since May 13 clearly shows the effect of the uncertainty over interest rates owing to the wide intra day movements by the index. The market's 10 day historical volatility has jumped up to 11.5 percent compared with 6.5 percent on May 13.

And although the index may have found a floor at 4,600 over the short-term, trendline resistance -- which is now at about 4,650 -- will halt any attempt at a rally. This trendline connects the FTSE's intra-day highs since May 16.
"The market's 10 day momentum is also beginning to slow and this confirms an overall weak trend," said one analyst who declined to be named. -- Pradip Mishra, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7954
